style.vernacular: Hindu Kush valley city at about 1,800 m: dense hillside neighbourhoods of flat-roofed mud-brick (pakhsa) and concrete-frame houses in dun, ochre and washed pastel render stacked up the slopes behind high courtyard walls, 1960s brutalist ministries and Soviet-style microrayon blocks, Amanullah-era Italianate stucco palaces and mosques, blue-tiled domes on the main shrines, and dusty poplar, mulberry and plane trees along the Kabul river.
style.ornament: Mughal and Timurid arched niches and jali screens; blue and turquoise glazed tile on domes and minarets; Amanullah-era Italianate stucco swags and pilasters ("Afghan Baroque"); carved timber door frames and balcony lattice; high mud-brick courtyard walls with blast barriers and razor-wire on modern compounds.

sources.what: cold semi-arid highland climate; hill neighbourhoods; 1960s brutalist ministries and Soviet-style microrayon estates; European-style Dilkusha palace; Shah-Do Shamshira
pakhsa (hand-laid earth) and sun-dried brick perimeter walls on stone foundations; planes, cypress, fruit trees; white marble mosque
yellow stucco, Italian-style ornament, "Afghan Baroque"
